document.title: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023 (SA 797 to S. 2226)
document.author: Chuck Schumer

passages.text: SA 797. Mr. SCHUMER (for himself, Mr. Rounds, Mr. Rubio, Mrs. Gillibrand, Mr. Young, and Mr. Heinrich) submitted an amendment intended to be proposed by him to the bill S. 2226, to authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2024 for military activities of the Department of Defense, for military construction, and for defense activities of the Department of Energy, to prescribe military personnel strengths for such fiscal year, and for other purposes; which was ordered to lie on the table; as follows:

(10) Legacy program.--The term ``legacy program'' means all Federal, State, and local government, commercial industry, academic, and private sector endeavors to collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence that pre-dates the date of the enactment of this Act.

(12) Non-human intelligence.--The term ``non-human intelligence'' means any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin that may be presumed responsible for unidentified anomalous phenomena or of which the Federal Government has become aware.

differs: In the Congressional Record of 13 July 2023 the amendment Schumer submitted for himself, Rounds, Rubio, Gillibrand, Young and Heinrich is printed on seven pages (S2953 to S2959) and uses the phrase "non-human intelligence" 24 times, headings included. The tellers do not say which print of the amendment they mean by 64 pages, or what they counted (22 times, or 65 times with UAP); if it is this text, the count of the phrase alone is 24.

passages.text: (a) Establishment.--There is established as an independent agency a board to be known as the ``Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board''.

(1) In general.--The President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, shall appoint, without regard to political affiliation, 9 citizens of the United States to serve as members of the Review Board to ensure and facilitate the review, transmission to the Archivist, and public disclosure of government records relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena.

t. The term 'special nuclear material' means (1) plutonium, uranium enriched in the isotope 233 or in the isotope 235, and any other material which the Commission, pursuant to the provisions of section 51, determines to be special nuclear material, but does not include source material; or (2) any material artificially enriched by any of the foregoing, but does not include source material.

SEC. 51. SPECIAL NUCLEAR MATERIAL.—The Commission may determine from time to time that other material is special nuclear material in addition to that specified in the definition as special nuclear material. Before making any such determination, the Commission must find that such material is capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy and must find that the determination that such material is special nuclear material is in the interest of the common defense and security, and the President must have expressly assented in writing to the determination.

differs: The tellers speak of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, and this is its text as enacted. It does not define special nuclear material as any material that releases atomic energy: it names plutonium and uranium enriched in the isotope 233 or 235, and any other material the Atomic Energy Commission declares special nuclear material after finding it "capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy", with the President's written assent. "Restricted Data" is defined as data (on atomic weapons, the production of special nuclear material and its use for energy), not material, and the words "born secret" do not occur in the act.

passages.text: b. OPERATION OF THE COMMISSION'S PRODUCTION FACILITIES.—The Commission is authorized and directed to produce or to provide for the production of special nuclear material in its own production facilities. To the extent deemed necessary, the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission. The Commission is also authorized to enter into research and development contracts authorizing the contractor to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission to the extent that the production of such special nuclear material may be incident to the conduct of research and development activities under such contracts.

quotes.quote: To the extent deemed necessary, the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission.

differs: The teller does not say which provision of the 1954 act he means; if it is section 41 b., the act lets the Atomic Energy Commission contract with others to produce special nuclear material, or to do research and development, in facilities the Commission owns. It says nothing of housing a craft or of any aerial object, and names no laboratory.

passages.text: The following notes are based on a set of five lectures given by R. Serber during the first two weeks of April 1943, as an "indoctrination course" in connection with the starting of the Los Alamos Project. The notes were written up by E. U. Condon.

The object of the project is to produce a practical military weapon in the form of a bomb in which the energy is released by a fast neutron chain reaction in one or more of the materials known to show nuclear fission.

differs: The Primer records that Condon wrote up Serber's April 1943 lectures at the start of the Los Alamos Project; it says nothing of who chose Los Alamos as the site.

passages.text: In accordance with President Donald Trump’s directive of March 17, 2025, all records previously withheld for classification that are part of the President John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Collection are released.
In an effort to maximize transparency, these records were released without redactions and some of these records contain the personal identification information of living individuals.
